These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0006] Record audit entry for every money movement: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver (FIN-2026-03): accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0010] Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes: For invalid monetary input raise BillingError from ledgerly.errors with a short snake_case code and the offending value as message, e.g. BillingError("non_positive_amount", str(amount)), matching ledgerly/payments.py.
  (learned from task S01 on ledgerly 2.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money inputs with round_money before storing: Always pass monetary values through `ledgerly.money.round_money` before storing them on models or comparing against `ZERO`; never store raw input Decimals.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integer arguments: When validating an integer parameter, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` are ints in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Normalize money inputs with round_money before storing Always pass monetary values through `ledgerly.money.round_money` before storing them on models or comparing against `ZERO`; never store raw input Decimals.
texts.at-0003: Use BillingError with snake_case codes Raise `ledgerly.errors.BillingError(code, detail)` with snake_case codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`; match the existing `invalid_state` message format `f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"`.
texts.at-0004: Reject bools when validating integer arguments When validating an integer parameter, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` are ints in Python.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
texts.at-0006: Record audit entry for every money movement Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
texts.at-0007: Accept idempotency_key and check it first Money-moving operations must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None and check it before state validation: if ledgerly.audit.events() has an entry with that key, return the original result without re-applying, and include idempotency_key in the audit entry
texts.at-0008: Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver (FIN-2026-03): accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing.
texts.at-0009: Money is Decimal end-to-end, never float In ledgerly, amounts must stay Decimal end-to-end with exactly two decimal places; convert inputs with `to_money`/`round_money` from `ledgerly.money` and never use float arithmetic. Convert rates or other numerics via `Decimal(str(x))` before multiplying a De
texts.at-0010: Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes For invalid monetary input raise BillingError from ledgerly.errors with a short snake_case code and the offending value as message, e.g. BillingError("non_positive_amount", str(amount)), matching ledgerly/payments.py.
texts.at-0011: Use Decimal, reject floats and bools Monetary and rate inputs are handled as Decimal; convert via Decimal(str(value)) and explicitly reject bool and float inputs rather than accepting them.

review_comments: [team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above the approval threshold need a second approver: accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing. The threshold is set by finance policy: 500.00 before 2.0.0, 1000.00 since 2.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

item.title: Support credit approval threshold is 1000.00
item.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-09 (2.0.0) sets the second-approver threshold for support-initiated refunds and credits at Decimal("1000.00"); amounts above it require an `approved_by` approver, amounts at or below it do not.
